title: Policy approval core
description: Objective: implement four-outcome policy evaluation, R0-R3 risk tiers, exact-hash approval decisions, and selective invalidation. Deliverable: packages/core policy modules with decision-table and property tests. NOT in scope: mutable UI policy editing, budgets, provider execution, or global speed modes. Hard dependencies: Runtime contract registry and Planning graph lifecycle core. Owned paths: packages/core/src/policy/**. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test.
definitionOfDone: Policy produces ALLOW, REQUIRE_APPROVAL, DENY, or HOLD_UNKNOWN with stable reason codes.
Unknown or missing inputs can never become ALLOW and caller risk labels cannot lower daemon-derived risk.
Approvals bind exact hashes/scope/policy/actor and invalidate only the proven impact set.
The focused core typecheck and test command exits 0.
taskRails: Follow the pinned design; this task cannot create authority beyond its named contract.
Fail closed with stable codes and immutable deterministic outputs.
Keep production modules focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400.
Use TDD and stage only explicit owned paths; no worktree, broad add, push, or merge.

implementationPlan.note:
REOPEN TRIAGE (read-only). QA's four issues verified against the landed code, not accepted on description alone:

1. policy-composition.ts:54-80 `ruleRelaxation` — CONFIRMED by reading. It compares `effect` (:59) and `obligations` (:61-78) only. `PolicyRule` (policy-contract.ts:80-85) has exactly four fields: `ruleId` (identity key of the fold map), `effect`, `obligations`, `requiredFactIds`. The fourth is never read by the detector.
2. policy-evaluation.ts:85 `assessEvidence` — CONFIRMED. It unions `rule.requiredFactIds` over `fold.rules`, and `foldSlices` (:113 `rules.set`) keeps the LAST declaration per ruleId. So a shrinking redeclaration deletes an ancestor's HOLD_UNKNOWN trigger while `relaxed` stays false. The escape is real and I am not disputing it.
3. policy-decision-table.test.ts:154 — CONFIRMED vacuous on this path. `rule()` (:31) defaults `requiredFactIds: []`; the only fixture that sets it is the top-level `input()` at :52. The field is never varied BETWEEN chain links anywhere in the suite.
4. policy-invariants.test.ts:16 — CONFIRMED. `buildInput` hard-codes `requiredFactIds: []` on both the root rule (:56) and the child redeclaration (:62), so the 320-seed sweep cannot emit a shrink.

No pushback on any item. QA's prescribed fix (a redeclared rule whose `requiredFactIds` is not a superset of the ancestor's is an unconditional, non-waivable relaxation) is the right shape: waivers resolve a `namedObligationId` to a SOFT obligation, and a required fact is not an obligation, so there is no waiver vocabulary that could cover this at all.

ARCHITECT NOTE acknowledged: fix in place, no rebuild, no re-split.

Conventions re-confirmed for this pass: no eslint config exists in the repo, so `tsc` + vitest are the whole machine gate; `noUnusedLocals`/`noUnusedParameters` are ON in tsconfig.base.json, which rules out a dangling type-level exhaustiveness alias (it would be reported as unused) — the monotonicity closure argument goes in a comment plus tests instead.

implementationPlan.note:
No change needed in `policy-contract.ts` or `policy-validation.ts` for this defect, and I checked rather than assumed.

The escape is in the composition detector, not in the shape guards. Two things verified in `policy-validation.ts` that the fix leans on:

1. `RULE_KEYS = ["effect", "obligations", "requiredFactIds", "ruleId"]` (:153) is consumed by `validRule` (:177) through `exact()`, which requires `Reflect.ownKeys(value).length === keys.length`. So a validated `PolicyRule` carries EXACTLY those four fields and no others. That is what makes the monotonicity closure argument checkable rather than a claim: `ruleId` is the fold's identity key and the remaining three are the whole authority surface, so a detector comparing effect + obligations + requiredFactIds compares the entire rule.

2. There is no waiver vocabulary that could ever cover a required fact. `validWaiver` (:197) requires `namedObligationId`, and the waiver path in `ruleRelaxation` only fires for an obligation the ancestor declared with `kind: "SOFT"`. A required fact is not an obligation and cannot be named as one, which is why QA's "unconditional, not waivable" is the only coherent reading — I encoded it as such rather than adding a waivable branch.

Consequence for future changes, recorded here because it is the actual lesson: adding a field to `PolicyRule` forces a `RULE_KEYS` edit (or every rule fails validation), and that edit is the moment to ask whether the new field is authority. The `exact()` guard is what turns "we might forget" into "the build makes you look".

No lines changed in this step.

GREEN. `pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/src/policy` -> 4 files / 37 tests passed; `pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck` exit 0.

Two changes, one per QA security finding, both at the file/line QA named.

(1) `policy-composition.ts` `ruleRelaxation` (QA issue 1). Added the required-fact comparison:
    const childFacts = new Set(child.requiredFactIds);
    let relaxed = effectRank(child.effect) < effectRank(ancestor.effect)
      || ancestor.requiredFactIds.some((factId) => !childFacts.has(factId));
Not-a-superset is an unconditional relaxation, sitting with the weakened effect rather than in the obligation loop, because the obligation loop is where the waiver branch lives and this must never reach it. Reasons a waiver cannot cover it are in the function comment, not just here: `validWaiver` requires a `namedObligationId` and the waiver branch only fires for an ancestor obligation with `kind: "SOFT"`. A required fact is neither, so there is no shape a caller could send that would make this waivable. That is asserted for three `namedObligationId` spellings in `policy-relaxation.test.ts`.

The comment also records the closure argument so the next person can re-check it in one read: `PolicyRule` has four fields, `validRule`'s `exact(value, RULE_KEYS)` guarantees no others exist, `ruleId` is the fold's identity key, and the other three are now all compared. The class QA said step-4's original note claimed closed is now actually closed, and checkably so.

(2) `policy-evaluation.ts` `assessEvidence` (QA issue 2). QA described this as a consequence of (1), and fixing (1) does close the reproduced escape. I did not leave it at that, because the dependency runs the wrong way: the evidence layer's refusal was only sound as long as the relaxation detector stayed complete. The required set is now unioned over EVERY slice in `input.sliceChain` instead of over `fold.rules` (the last declaration of each ruleId).

Behaviour is unchanged for every legal chain — a child may only widen, so union == fold — and an illegal chain is already DENY from layer 2. What changes is the failure mode: both layers must now regress before a shrunken redeclaration can reach ALLOW, instead of one. The `assessEvidence` signature lost its `rules` parameter; it reads the chain directly.

Adversarial check on my own change: added rules can only tighten. `assessRules` starts at ALLOW and folds through `dominant`, which never descends, and a new rule's `requiredFactIds` enters the evidence union. So a child that ADDS a rule or widens a required set cannot lower any outcome — verified by the widened-redeclaration case, which stays ALLOW when the added fact is supplied and HOLD_UNKNOWN (not DENY) when it is absent.

Sizes after the change: policy-composition.ts 133, policy-evaluation.ts 202. Both well under 250.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red then green — src/policy/approval-invalidation.test.ts + src/policy/approval-invalidation.ts (each <=250). Approval lifecycle: PENDING -> DECIDED|WITHDRAWN (WITHDRAWN terminal, no outgoing edges); decision APPROVE|REJECT immutable once DECIDED; validity projection CURRENT -> INVALIDATED | SUPERSEDED, never backward. SELECTIVE INVALIDATION (DoD 3): takes a SUPPLIED deterministic impact set (the graph diff computation is the scheduler/daemon's job per design 265 — validate-and-apply only): invalidates ONLY approvals whose bound hashes/scope intersect the impact set — non-intersecting approvals BIT-IDENTICAL after (property-asserted); impact-set input inherits the unknown-canonicalization refusal (design 250/265: hashes carry canonicalizer versions; unknown version -> refuse, fail closed). SUPERSEDED path: applied ONLY via an explicit successor-approval linkage input (a new revision's approval marks its predecessor SUPERSEDED — design 263/269 'old approval bytes are never relabeled'), DISTINCT from impact-set intersection -> INVALIDATED. Carry-forward invalidation conditions per design 265, all six: any mismatch, missing dependency, changed applicable policy slice, changed predecessor result, changed environment/runtime closure, unknown canonicalization -> carry-forward INVALID. Lifecycle rejections: ILLEGAL_TRANSITION from {aggregate:'APPROVAL'} with exact-code assertions (this test file is where the silent-degrade assertions live). Both files green.

implementationPlan.note:
QA issue 4 closed. `policy-invariants.test.ts` 250 lines (was 240); typecheck exit 0; `pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/src/policy` -> 4 files / 37 tests passed.

Generator bias (the vacuity fix). `buildInput` now varies the required-fact set BETWEEN links instead of hard-coding `[]` on both:
  const rootRequired = rand() < 0.55 ? FACT_IDS.filter(() => rand() < 0.6) : [];
  const draw = rand();
  const childRequired = draw < 0.35 ? rootRequired.slice(1)
    : draw < 0.6 ? [...new Set([...rootRequired, pick(FACT_IDS)])] : rootRequired;
Three shapes — shrink, widen, keep — so the sweep exercises both directions of monotonicity, not only the one that now fails closed.

Detection is derived from the input, not from generator bookkeeping: `shrinksRequiredFacts` reads the chain's two links and reports whether the redeclaration dropped an ancestor's fact. A generator retune cannot silently desynchronise a counter from what it actually emitted.

NON-VACUITY REPORT, measured on the landed suite (temporary forced-fail assertion, run, reverted; `git status` confirms no probe left behind):
  outcomes over 320 seeds — HOLD_UNKNOWN 169, DENY 74, REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL 67, ALLOW 10
  unusable-required-fact seeds: 222
  SHRINK-SHAPE seeds: 10  (was 0 — the shape QA proved unreachable)
All four outcomes and all four tiers still reached, so widening the generator did not collapse the ALLOW branch it needs to keep hitting.

Every shrink seed now asserts the property directly, not merely "not ALLOW": `expect(decision).toBe("DENY")` plus `toContain("SLICE_RELAXATION_DETECTED")`. The floor assertion is `expect(shrunk).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(5)` with the observed 10/320 recorded beside it — a `> 0` floor would let a future retune drift to a single seed and still pass, which is how this got here.

`hasUnusableRequiredFact` now unions the required set over every slice's rules plus the top-level list. Previously it read only `input.requiredFactIds`, so invariant (1) never looked at rule-declared facts at all — the sweep could not have caught the escape even with a biased generator. It now states the spec-level property: a fact ANY link demanded must be usable or the decision is not ALLOW (dropped -> DENY via layer 2, still demanded -> HOLD_UNKNOWN via layer 1).

Also removed a vacuous assertion found while working here: `expect(POLICY_OUTCOMES.indexOf(result.record.decision)).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0)` in the waiver-laundering test cannot fail for any valid outcome.

Size: the file was 240 and these additions ran it to 263, so I compressed comments and collapsed a four-line null-tier branch to reach exactly 250. No assertion was dropped to make room.

(2) GATE: `pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test` -> exit 0, 13 files / 226 tests. Run TWICE, identical counts (570ms / 518ms). Repo-wide `pnpm test` -> 109 files, 1549 passed | 1 skipped, ZERO failures, so nothing to attribute by path.

(4) createRuntimeError call sites unchanged at three, all `INPUT_INVALID` sourceless or the APPROVAL-sourced ILLEGAL_TRANSITION in approval-invalidation. No new call site, so no new silent-degrade surface.

ADVERSARIAL RED-TEAM of my own diff (the four laundering paths, re-run against the fixed code):
(a) Shrink via a DIFFERENT ruleId — a child declaring a new rule cannot remove the parent's, since the fold never deletes a ruleId; the parent's required facts stay in both the effective set and the union. Refused.
(b) Shrink via an intra-slice duplicate — two rules with the same ruleId inside ONE slice hit the same `rules.get(ruleId) !== undefined` branch, so the second is compared against the first. Refused, no special case needed.
(c) Waiver over a shrink — asserted for three `namedObligationId` spellings (fact ID, rule ID, real SOFT obligation). The waiver branch is reachable only from the ancestor-obligation loop, and a required fact never enters it. Refused.
(d) Hint or opt-in rescuing a shrink — DENY dominates every outcome those layers can produce. Refused.
(e) Overshoot check (the opposite failure): a child ADDING a required fact must not be slandered as a relaxation. Asserted explicitly — widened with the fact present is ALLOW, widened with it absent is HOLD_UNKNOWN and specifically NOT SLICE_RELAXATION_DETECTED.
(f) Hostile input — both new loops read the SNAPSHOTTED, validated structure (`validateEvaluationInput` returns the snapshot), so no accessor or proxy is reachable from them. `new Set(child.requiredFactIds)` is local, no shared state, no mutation of caller data.
(g) Determinism — the required-set iteration order changed (chain order, not fold order), which cannot matter: `reasonCodes` is a sorted Set and `outcome` folds through an order-independent lattice. Confirmed by the two identical runs.
(h) Complexity — assessEvidence is now O(slices x rules) instead of O(distinct rules). Same order as the fold that already runs beside it; no new unbounded loop.
(i) No scratch files: `git status --porcelain -- packages` returns empty. The forced-fail probe used to read the non-vacuity counts was an in-file assertion, reverted, not a probe file.

failedDodItems: Unknown or missing inputs can never become ALLOW and caller risk labels cannot lower daemon-derived risk.

issues.description: ruleRelaxation compares a child redeclaration against its ancestor on `effect` (:59) and `obligations` (:62-78) only, never on `requiredFactIds`, so a child redeclaring a parent ruleId with a reduced requiredFactIds leaves `relaxed` false and emits no SLICE_RELAXATION_DETECTED. Fix: a redeclared rule whose requiredFactIds is not a superset of the ancestor's is an unconditional relaxation, like a dropped HARD obligation (not waivable; waivers cover named SOFT obligations only).

assessEvidence derives the required-fact set from fold.rules, the LAST declaration of each ruleId (policy-composition.ts:113). With the gap above this is a live HOLD_UNKNOWN -> ALLOW escape. Reproduced: chain [root] with rule.audit requiredFactIds ["fact.audit"] and fact.audit absent -> HOLD_UNKNOWN/REQUIRED_FACT_MISSING; appending a child redeclaring rule.audit with requiredFactIds [] -> ALLOW/ALLOWED_BY_POLICY. Violates DoD 2 and design 699.

The relaxation loop covers four shapes (effect weakened, HARD obligation dropped, HARD->SOFT downgrade, uncovered child opt-in) but never varies requiredFactIds across slices — the rule() helper at :31 defaults it to [] and only the single-slice fixture at :52 sets it. Add a fifth entry whose child redeclares the parent ruleId with a shrunken requiredFactIds and assert decision === "DENY" plus SLICE_RELAXATION_DETECTED.

The 320-seed sweep passes vacuously on this path: the generator never emits a redeclaration that shrinks a rule's required-fact set, so invariant (1) 'no seed reaches ALLOW with a missing required fact' never exercises the escape. Bias the chain generator so at least one seed shrinks a redeclared rule's requiredFactIds, and re-report the non-vacuity counts in the step note.

reviewSummary:
APPROVE — all four issues from reopen #1 fixed. Verified independently, not from the notes.

GATE re-run: typecheck exit 0; `pnpm --filter @moe/core test` exit 0, 13 files / 226 tests — matches the filed outputTail (was 12/221; delta is the new policy-relaxation.test.ts).

MY OWN PROBE, written fresh, run, deleted (`git status --porcelain -- packages/core` clean after):
- A, prior QA's exact repro (child redeclares rule.audit with requiredFactIds []): was ALLOW, now {"decision":"DENY","reasonCodes":["REQUIRED_FACT_MISSING","SLICE_RELAXATION_DETECTED"]}.
- B, duplicate ruleId INSIDE one slice, second declaration empty — an angle their tests miss: DENY + both codes.
- C, child omits the ancestor rule entirely: HOLD_UNKNOWN/REQUIRED_FACT_MISSING, correctly no relaxation code, fact still required via the chain-wide union.
- D, three links where the leaf shrinks against the running effective rule: DENY.

MUTATION — did not trust the tests to be load-bearing. Stripped the ancestor.requiredFactIds.some(...) clause from ruleRelaxation: 6 tests failed across 3 files (relaxation, decision-table, invariants). Reverted, tree clean, gate green.

ISSUE BY ISSUE: (1) policy-composition.ts:54 treats a shrunken required-fact set as an unconditional, non-waivable relaxation. (2) assessEvidence unions required facts over every slice instead of the fold's last-declaration set — defense in depth, both layers must regress. (3) decision-table gained the shrink case. (4) invariants generator emits the shape with a non-vacuity floor, expect(shrunk).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(5), comment recording 10/320 — a canary against a silent generator retune.

DoD 2 second half re-checked: a hint raises effectiveTier but never computedTier, usedFactIds or inputFacts. Purity grep: 3 hits, all prose in headers, zero in code. All 11 policy files <=250.

Size: prior QA scoped it out for this task; honored rather than move goalposts mid-fix.
